basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Covers the standing capability to deliver health services, not individual encounters or clinical content.
Publishes offerings, availability, capacity and access conditions that patients and referrers act on.
Contains health care encounters as child records but does not own diagnoses, orders or treatment.
Separate from practitioner licensure and facility construction, which it references.

may: Publish service offerings, opening hours and access conditions from the authoritative directory.
Report available capacity and queue status to authorized referrers.
Help a person find a service that matches stated needs and eligibility.
Flag inconsistencies between published offerings and practitioner role bindings.
mustNot: Give diagnosis or treatment advice under the guise of service navigation.
Allocate or withhold scarce capacity on criteria not set by the governing authority.
Publish availability that has not been confirmed by the provider.
Disclose identifiable patient data in queue or capacity reports.
Steer patients to services for commercial reasons.
requiresHuman: Changing triage, prioritization or eligibility rules for access.
Suspending or withdrawing a service that patients depend on.
Committing capacity under contracts with commissioners or insurers.

considerations: Access rules and capacity allocation decide who gets care first; they must be fair and explainable.
Wrong availability information can delay urgent care.
Aggregate service data can still reveal sensitive information about small patient groups.
People with disabilities or language needs must find accurate access information.

items: A health care delivery record names a provider organization, a service offering, a location, access conditions and capacity.
It is confused with an encounter, an appointment slot and a facility record.
Delayed treatment when patients are sent to a service that is unavailable.
Unfair rationing hidden in opaque access rules.
Re-identification from small-number capacity or queue data.
Overload of a service through uncoordinated referrals.
HL7 FHIR Schedule, Slot and Endpoint resources.
IHE Mobile Care Services Discovery (mCSD) profile.
SNOMED CT for service type coding.
ISO/TS 22220 for subject of care identification.
